sentences.zh: 廣順元年冬十月己丑朔，宰臣王峻獻唐張蘊古《大寶箴》、謝偃《惟皇誡德賦》二圖。

translations.literal: On the jichou new moon of the tenth month in winter, Guangshun year 1, Chief Minister Wang Jun presented two illustrated works from Tang: Zhang Yungu's Great Treasure Admonition and Xie Yan's Admonition on the Emperor's Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou new moon in the tenth month of winter, Guangshun 1, Chief Minister Wang Jun presented two Tang-era illustrated texts: Zhang Yungu's Great Treasure Admonition and Xie Yan's Admonition on the Emperor's Virtue.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「朕生長軍戎，勤勞南北，雖用心於《鈐》、《匱》，且無暇於《詩》、《書》，世務時艱，粗經閱歷，前言往行，未甚討尋。

translations.literal: An edict in reply said: "I grew up amid armies and toiled north and south; though I applied myself to the military manuals Qian and Kui, I had no leisure for the Odes and Documents; the affairs of the age and their hardships I have only roughly experienced, and the words and deeds of former ages I have not much investigated."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied by edict: "I was raised in the military and labored north and south; though I studied the war manuals Qian and Kui, I never had time for the Odes and Documents; I have only a rough acquaintance with the troubles of the times and have scarcely explored the wisdom of the past."

sentences.zh: 卿有佐命立國之勛，居代天調鼎之任，恒慮眇德，未及古人。

translations.literal: "You have merit in aiding the Mandate and founding the state, and hold the charge of regulating the realm on Heaven's behalf; I always fear my slight virtue falls short of the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: "You aided the founding of the dynasty and now regulate the realm in Heaven's stead; I constantly worry that my limited virtue cannot match the ancients."

sentences.zh: 於是采掇箴規，弼諧寡昧，披文閱理，懌意怡神，究為君治國之源，審修己御人之要。

translations.literal: "Therefore you gathered admonitions and regulations to assist my dim understanding; reading the text and examining its principles delights the mind and settles the spirit, probing the source of governing the state as ruler and discerning the essentials of cultivating oneself and commanding others."
translations.idiomatic: "You have gathered these admonitions to guide my ignorance; reading them delights the spirit and clarifies the roots of rulership and the essentials of self-cultivation and governing others."

sentences.zh: 帝王之道，盡在於茲，辭翰俱高，珠寶何貴！

translations.literal: "The Way of emperors and kings is all here—both writings are lofty; what treasure could be more precious!"
translations.idiomatic: "The way of kings is fully contained in these works—both texts are superb; no jewel could be more valuable!"

sentences.zh: 再三省覽，深用愧嘉。

translations.literal: "On repeated examination I am deeply moved to shame and approval."
translations.idiomatic: "I have read them again and again and am deeply moved—both humbled and grateful."

sentences.zh: 其所進圖，已令於行坐處張懸，所冀出入看讀，用為鑒戒。

translations.literal: "The illustrations you presented have been ordered hung where I walk and sit, so that passing in and out I may read them as a mirror and warning."
translations.idiomatic: "I have ordered your illustrations hung where I pass my days, so that I may read them coming and going and take them as my mirror and warning."

sentences.zh: 」壬辰，潞州奏，巡檢使陳思讓、監軍向訓破河東賊軍於虒亭。

translations.literal: On renchen, Luzhou reported: Inspector Chen Siyang and army supervisor Xiang Xun defeated Hedong rebel forces at Sixiting.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Luzhou reported that inspector Chen Siyang and army supervisor Xiang Xun had routed Hedong rebels at Sixiting.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以刑部侍郎司徒詡為戶部侍郎，以左散騎常侍張煦為刑部侍郎，以給事中呂咸休為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On guisi, Vice Minister of Punishments Situ Xu was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Zhang Xu was made Vice Minister of Punishments; and Secretariat Drafter Lü Xianxiu was made Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Situ Xu moved from Punishments to Revenue; Zhang Xu took Punishments; and Lü Xianxiu became Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 甲午，絳州防禦使孫漢英卒。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Jiangzhou defense commissioner Sun Hanying died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Jiangzhou defense commissioner Sun Hanying died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，荊南奏，湖南亂，大將軍陸孟俊執偽節度使馬希萼遷於衡州，立希萼弟希崇為留後，將吏二千餘人，遇害者半，牙署庫藏焚燒殆盡。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Jingnan reported: Hunan is in turmoil; Grand General Lu Mengjun seized the puppet military governor Ma Xie and moved him to Hengzhou, installing Xie's brother Xichong as acting commissioner; of more than two thousand officers and clerks, half were killed, and the headquarters treasury was burned nearly clean.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Jingnan reported turmoil in Hunan: Grand General Lu Mengjun seized puppet governor Ma Xie, exiled him to Hengzhou, and installed his brother Xichong; of over two thousand officials and troops, half were killed and the headquarters treasury was nearly burned out.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔並吏部三銓為一銓，委本司長官通判。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict merged the Ministry of Personnel's three review boards into one, entrusting joint adjudication to the ministry's chief.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi an edict combined the Personnel Ministry's three selection boards into one, with the ministry chief overseeing all reviews.

sentences.zh: 丙午，晉州巡檢王萬敢奏，河東劉崇入寇，營於州北。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Jinzhou inspector Wang Wangan reported: Hedong's Liu Chong invaded and encamped north of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Jinzhou inspector Wang Wangan reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had invaded and camped north of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，潞州奏，河東賊軍寇境。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Luzhou reported Hedong rebel forces raiding the border.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Luzhou reported Hedong rebel raids on the border.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，荊南奏，淮南遣鄂州節度使劉仁贍，以戰船二百艘於今月二十五日入岳州。

translations.literal: On yimao, Jingnan reported: Huainan sent Ezhou military governor Liu Renzan with two hundred warships, which entered Yuezhou on the twenty-fifth of this month.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Jingnan reported that Huainan had sent Ezhou governor Liu Renzan with two hundred warships into Yuezhou on the twenty-fifth of this month.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔樞密使王峻率兵援晉州。

translations.literal: On bingchen, an edict ordered Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun to lead troops to relieve Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen an edict ordered Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun to march to Jinzhou's relief.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以左衛將軍申師厚為河西軍節度使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Left Guard General Shen Shihou was made military governor of the Hexi Army and Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Left Guard general Shen Shihou was appointed Hexi military governor and acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 師厚素與王峻善，及峻貴，師厚羈旅無依，日於峻馬前望塵而拜，會西涼請帥，帝令擇之，無欲去者，峻乃以師厚奏之，師厚亦欣然求往，尋自前鎮將授左衛將軍、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Shihou had long been friendly with Wang Jun; when Jun rose to power, Shihou, destitute and without support, daily bowed to him in the dust before his horse. When Liangzhou requested a commander, the Emperor ordered a selection, but none wished to go; Jun therefore recommended Shihou, and Shihou also gladly sought the post; shortly before he had been appointed from his former post as Left Guard General and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou and Wang Jun were old friends; after Jun's rise, the homeless Shihou bowed to him in the dust before his horse every day. When the Western Liang post opened and no one wanted it, Jun nominated Shihou, who eagerly accepted—he had just been made Left Guard general and acting Works minister.

sentences.zh: 翌日，乃有涼州之命，賜旌節、駝馬、繒帛以遣之。

translations.literal: The next day came the appointment to Liangzhou, and he was sent off with banners of authority, camels, horses, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he received the Liangzhou appointment and was sent off with insignia, camels, horses, and silks.

sentences.zh: 十一月己未朔，荊南奏，淮南大將邊鎬率兵三萬，自袁州路趨潭州，馬希崇遣從事送牌印，納器仗。

translations.literal: On the jiwei new moon of the eleventh month, Jingnan reported: Huainan's Grand General Bian Hao led thirty thousand troops from the Yuanzhou route toward Tanzhou; Ma Xichong sent an aide to deliver seals and insignia and surrender weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei new moon in the eleventh month, Jingnan reported that Huainan general Bian Hao was marching thirty thousand men from Yuanzhou toward Tanzhou while Ma Xichong sent an envoy to surrender his seals and arms.

sentences.zh: 鎬入城，稱武安軍節度使，馬氏諸族及將吏千餘人皆徙於金陵。

translations.literal: Hao entered the city and styled himself military governor of the Wu'an Army; more than a thousand of the Ma clan and their officers and clerks were all relocated to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Hao entered the city as Wu'an military governor and relocated over a thousand Ma clansmen and officials to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 甲子夜，東南白虹亙天。

translations.literal: On the night of jiazi, a white rainbow stretched across the sky in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: That night a white rainbow spanned the southeastern sky.

sentences.zh: 以新晉州節度使王彥超為晉絳行營馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Jinzhou military governor Wang Yanchao was made chief adjutant of cavalry for the Jin-Jiang campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: New Jinzhou governor Wang Yanchao was named chief cavalry adjutant of the Jin-Jiang campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，命王峻出征晉州，帝幸西莊以餞之。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wang Jun was ordered to campaign to Jinzhou; the Emperor went to the Western Villa to give him a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Wang Jun was sent to Jinzhou; the Emperor saw him off with a feast at the Western Villa.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，日南至，群臣拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the winter solstice; the ministers presented memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the winter solstice, the court offered congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 甲申，葬故貴妃張氏。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the late Honored Consort Zhang was buried.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the late Honored Consort Zhang was interred.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔：「唐朝五廟，舊在至德宮安置，應屬徽陵莊田園舍，宜令新除右監門將軍李重玉為主。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict said: "The five temples of the Tang dynasty, formerly housed in the Zhide Palace, with estates and gardens belonging to Huiling—Li Chongyu, newly appointed General of the Right Gate Guards, should be made custodian."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict appointed the newly made Right Gate Guards general Li Chongyu custodian of the Tang five temples at Zhide Palace and their Huiling estates.

sentences.zh: 其緣陵緣廟法物，除合留外，所有金銀器物，充遷葬故淑妃王氏及許王從益外，其餘並給與重玉及尼惠英、惠燈、惠能、惠嚴等。

translations.literal: Of ritual objects pertaining to the tombs and temples, aside from what should be retained, all gold and silver vessels, except those needed to relocate the burial of the late Shufei Wang and Prince Xu Congyi, were to be given to Chongyu and the nuns Huiying, Huideng, Huineng, Huiyan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Temple and tomb ritual goods were to be distributed: gold and silver vessels needed for relocating Shufei Wang and Prince Xu Congyi were reserved; the rest went to Chongyu and the nuns Huiying, Huideng, Huineng, and Huiyan.

sentences.zh: 令重玉以時祀陵廟，務在豐潔。

translations.literal: "Chongyu was ordered to sacrifice at the tombs and temples on schedule, with offerings to be ample and pure."
translations.idiomatic: "Chongyu was charged to maintain timely, generous sacrifices at the tombs and temples."

sentences.zh: 」重玉，故皇城使李從璨之子，明宗之孫，惠英等亦明宗親屬也，故帝授重玉官秩，令主先祀，恤王者之後也。

translations.literal: Chongyu was the son of the late Imperial City Commissioner Li Congcan and grandson of Emperor Mingzong; Huiying and the others were also Mingzong's kin. Therefore the Emperor granted Chongyu rank and ordered him to preside over the former sacrifices—showing compassion for the descendants of kings.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu was the grandson of Mingzong through Li Congcan; the nuns were Mingzong kin as well. The Emperor gave Chongyu office so he could tend the former rites—mercy toward a fallen dynasty's line.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊子朔，詔以劉崇入寇，取當月三日暫幸西京。

translations.literal: On the wuzi new moon of the twelfth month, an edict because Liu Chong had invaded set the third day of the month for a temporary visit to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi new moon in the twelfth month, an edict scheduled a temporary visit to the Western Capital on the third, because Liu Chong had invaded.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔巡幸宜停。

translations.literal: On gengyin, an edict ordered the tour halted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin an edict canceled the tour.

sentences.zh: 時王峻駐軍陜府，聞帝西巡，遣使馳奏，不勞車駕順動，帝乃止。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jun was encamped at Shan Prefecture; hearing the Emperor would tour west, he sent a messenger in haste to report that there was no need for the imperial carriage to move, and the Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, camped at Shan Prefecture, heard of the western tour and urgently petitioned that the Emperor need not come; the Emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 乙未，幸西莊。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the Emperor visited the Western Villa.

sentences.zh: 兗州慕容彥超上言，乞朝覲，詔允之，尋稱部內草寇起，不敢離鎮。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao of Yanzhou memorialized requesting an audience; an edict approved it, but soon he claimed bandits had risen within his circuit and dared not leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou's Murong Yanchao asked to attend court and was approved, then claimed bandit unrest and refused to leave his post.

sentences.zh: 戊申，鄆州奏，慕容彥超據城反。

translations.literal: On wushen, Yunzhou reported Murong Yanchao had seized the city and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Yunzhou reported that Murong Yanchao had rebelled and held the city.

sentences.zh: 己酉，王峻奏，劉崇逃遁，王師已入晉州。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wang Jun reported Liu Chong had fled and the imperial army had entered Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Wang Jun reported Liu Chong's flight and the imperial army's entry into Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·陳思讓傳》：王峻援晉州，以思讓與康延昭分為左右廂排陣使，令率軍自烏嶺路至絳州，與大軍合。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Chen Siyang: When Wang Jun relieved Jinzhou, he made Siyang and Kang Yanzhao left and right wing formation commanders, ordering them to lead troops from Wuling Road to Jiangzhou to join the main army.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Song History biography of Chen Siyang: Wang Jun, relieving Jinzhou, appointed Siyang and Kang Yanzhao left and right wing commanders and ordered them from Wuling Road to Jiangzhou to join the main force.

sentences.zh: 崇燒營遁去，思讓又與藥元福襲破之。）〉

translations.literal: Chong burned his camp and fled; Siyang again joined with Yao Yuanfu to strike and defeat him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Chong burned his camp and fled; Siyang and Yao Yuanfu then routed him in a joint attack.)〉

sentences.zh: 廣順二年春正月戊午朔，不受朝賀，以宿兵在外故也。

translations.literal: On the wuwu new moon of the first month in spring, Guangshun year 2, court congratulations were not received, because troops were still encamped abroad.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu new moon in spring, Guangshun 2, the court skipped New Year congratulations because troops were still in the field.

sentences.zh: 庚申，王峻奏，起近鎮丁夫二萬城晉州。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wang Jun reported raising twenty thousand corvée laborers from nearby prefectures to fortify Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Wang Jun reported drafting twenty thousand laborers from nearby prefectures to wall Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，修東京羅城，凡役丁夫五萬五千，兩旬而罷。

translations.literal: On renxu, the outer wall of the Eastern Capital was repaired; fifty-five thousand corvée laborers were employed, and the work ceased after twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Eastern Capital's outer wall was repaired with fifty-five thousand laborers; the project finished in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英為兗州行營都部署，以齊州防禦使史延韜為副部署，以皇城使向訓為兵馬都監，陳州防禦使藥元福為馬步都虞候，率兵討慕容彥超。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Palace Foot Army Commander-in-Chief Cao Ying was made overall commander of the Yanzhou campaign headquarters; Qizhou defense commissioner Shi Yantao was made deputy commander; Imperial City Commissioner Xiang Xun was made overall army inspector; Chenzhou defense commissioner Yao Yuanfu was made chief adjutant of horse and foot; they led troops to suppress Murong Yanchao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Cao Ying was named Yanzhou campaign commander, Shi Yantao his deputy, Xiang Xun army inspector, and Yao Yuanfu chief adjutant, to march against Murong Yanchao.

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》：慕容彥超盜據兗、海，周祖命曹英為帥，向訓副之，參用藥元福以兵從。

translations.literal: (Longping Collection: Murong Yanchao seized Yan and Hai by force; the Zhou founder appointed Cao Ying commander, with Xiang Xun as deputy, and employed Yao Yuanfu with troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Longping Collection: Murong Yanchao held Yan and Hai; Taizu named Cao Ying commander, Xiang Xun deputy, and Yao Yuanfu to accompany the army.

sentences.zh: 謂元福曰：「已敕英、訓，勿以軍禮見汝。

translations.literal: He said to Yuanfu: "I have already ordered Ying and Xun not to receive you with military ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: He told Yuanfu: "I have instructed Ying and Xun not to treat you with military deference."

sentences.zh: 」及元福至，英、訓皆父事焉。）〉

translations.literal: "When Yuanfu arrived, both Ying and Xun treated him as a father.)〉
translations.idiomatic: "When Yuanfu arrived, Ying and Xun both honored him as a father figure.)〉

sentences.zh: 諸軍入兗州界，不得下路停止村舍，犯者以軍法從事。

translations.literal: When the armies entered Yanzhou territory, they were forbidden to leave the road and lodge in villages; violators were dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Troops entering Yanzhou were forbidden to leave the road or billet in villages; violators faced military justice.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，徐州巡檢供給官張令彬奏，破淮賊於沭陽，斬首千餘級，擒賊將燕敬權。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Xuzhou inspector and supply officer Zhang Lingbin reported defeating Huai rebels at Shuyang, beheading more than a thousand, and capturing the rebel general Yan Jingquan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Xuzhou inspector Zhang Lingbin reported a victory at Shuyang over Huai rebels—over a thousand heads and the capture of general Yan Jingquan.

sentences.zh: 時慕容彥超求援於淮南，淮南偽主李景發兵援之，師於下邳，聞官軍至，退趨沭陽，遂破之。

translations.literal: At the time Murong Yanchao sought aid from Huainan; the Huainan puppet ruler Li Jing sent troops to support him, encamped at Xiapi, and on hearing the imperial army had arrived, withdrew toward Shuyang and was there defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao had asked Huainan for help; Li Jing sent reinforcements to Xiapi, but they retreated toward Shuyang when the imperial army arrived and were defeated there.

sentences.zh: 庚午，高麗權知國事王昭遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Wang Zhao, acting administrator of Goryeo affairs, sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Goryeo's acting regent Wang Zhao sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 壬申，鎮州何福進差人部送先擒獲到河東賊軍二百餘人至闕下，詔給巾履衫袴以釋之。

translations.literal: On renshen, He Fujin of Zhenzhou dispatched men escorting more than two hundred Hedong rebel soldiers previously captured to the capital; an edict gave them caps, shoes, shirts, and trousers and released them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Zhenzhou's He Fujin sent over two hundred captured Hedong rebels to court; they were given clothing and released.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，徐州部送沭陽所獲賊將燕敬權等四人至闕下，詔賜衣服金帛，放歸本土，敬權等感泣謝罪。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Xuzhou escorted to the capital the rebel generals Yan Jingquan and three others captured at Shuyang; an edict bestowed clothing and gold and silks and sent them home; Jingquan and the others wept with gratitude and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Xuzhou delivered Yan Jingquan and three other Shuyang captives; clothed and rewarded, they were sent home weeping thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝召見謂之曰：「夫惡兇邪，獎忠順，天下一也。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned them and said: "To hate the vicious and evil and reward the loyal and obedient is one principle throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received them and said: "Punishing the wicked and rewarding loyalty is the same principle everywhere under heaven."

sentences.zh: 我之賊臣，撓亂國法，嬰城作逆，殃及生靈，不意吳人助茲兇惡，非良算也，爾當歸言之於爾君。

translations.literal: "My rebel subject disturbed the laws of the state, held the city in rebellion, and brought calamity on the people; I did not expect the Wu people to aid such villainy—it is no wise plan. You should return and report this to your lord."
translations.idiomatic: "Our rebel defied the law, walled himself in, and harmed the people; I did not expect Wu to aid such evil—it is poor strategy. Go tell your lord what I say."

sentences.zh: 」初，漢末遣三司軍將路昌祚於湖南市茶，屬淮南將邊鎬陷長沙，昌祚被賊送金陵。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Han, the Commission of the Three Departments had sent army officer Lu Changzuo to Hunan to purchase tea; when Huainan general Bian Hao captured Changsha, Changzuo was sent by the rebels to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, late in Han, Lu Changzuo had been sent to Hunan to buy tea; when Bian Hao took Changsha, the rebels sent Changzuo to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 及敬權自大朝歸，具以帝言告於李景，景乃召昌祚，延坐從容久之，且稱美大朝皇帝聖德廣被，恩沾鄰土，深有依附國家之意。

translations.literal: When Jingquan returned from the great court, he fully reported the Emperor's words to Li Jing; Jing then summoned Changzuo, seated him at ease for a long while, and praised the great court Emperor's sagely virtue spreading widely, his grace reaching neighboring lands, and his deep intent to draw the state close.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingquan returned, he repeated the Emperor's message to Li Jing, who summoned Changzuo, entertained him at length, and praised the Zhou Emperor's virtue and his wish to draw neighbors near.

sentences.zh: 及罷，遣偽宰相宋齊丘宴昌祚於別館，又令訪昌祚在湖南遭變之時，亡失綱運之數，命依數償之，給茗荈萬八千斤，遣水運至江夏，仍厚給行裝，遣之歸闕。

translations.literal: When the audience ended, he sent his puppet chancellor Song Qiqiu to feast Changzuo at a separate lodge, and also ordered inquiry into how much of the tea transport Changzuo had lost when disaster struck in Hunan; he commanded repayment according to the amount, gave eighteen thousand jin of tea, sent it by water transport to Jiangxia, still generously provided travel gear, and sent him back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Song Qiqiu feasted Changzuo; Jing inquired how much tea cargo had been lost in Hunan, repaid the full amount, gave eighteen thousand jin of tea shipped to Jiangxia, furnished generous travel expenses, and sent him home to court.

sentences.zh: 二月庚寅，府州防卸使折德扆奏，河東賊軍寇境，率州兵破之，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengyin, Fuzhou defense commissioner Zhe Deyi reported Hedong rebel forces raiding the border; he led prefectural troops to defeat them and took two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengyin, Fuzhou's Zhe Deyi reported repelling a Hedong raid with two thousand enemy killed.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，太白經天。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Venus crossed the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Venus crossed the sky.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以權知高麗國事王昭為高麗國王。

translations.literal: On guisi, Wang Zhao, acting administrator of Goryeo affairs, was made King of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi acting Goryeo regent Wang Zhao was enthroned as king.

sentences.zh: 庚子，府州防卸使折德扆奏，收河東界岢嵐軍。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Fuzhou defense commissioner Zhe Deyi reported recovering Kelan Army on the Hedong border.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Zhe Deyi reported recovering the Kelan garrison on the Hedong frontier.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔先獲河東鄉軍一百餘人，各給錢鞋放歸鄉里。

translations.literal: On guimao, an edict ordered that more than a hundred Hedong militiamen previously captured each be given money and shoes and released to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao over a hundred captured Hedong militiamen were given money and shoes and sent home.

sentences.zh: 壬子，太子太師致仕安審暉卒。

translations.literal: On renzi, retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent An Shenhui died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi retired Grand Mentor An Shenhui died.

sentences.zh: 三月庚申，幸南莊，令從臣習射。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengshen, the Emperor visited the Southern Villa and ordered his attendants to practice archery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen, the Emperor visited the Southern Villa for archery practice with his court.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以樞密院直學士、左諫議大夫王溥為中書舍人，充翰林學士；

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wang Pu, academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Left Remonstrance Grand Master, was made Secretariat Drafter and appointed Hanlin Academician;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wang Pu was made Secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以內客省使、恩州團練使鄭仁誨為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Inner Reception Commissioner and Enzhou regimental trainer Zheng Renhui was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and Zheng Renhui became vice military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔宣徽北院使翟光鄴權知永興軍府事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Northern Palace Secretariat Commissioner Zhai Guangye to act as administrator of Yongxing military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Zhai Guangye acting administrator of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，回鶻遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Uyghurs sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Uyghur envoys brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔：「西京莊宅司、內侍省、宮苑司、內園等四司，所管諸巡系稅戶二千五百並還府縣。

translations.literal: On gengchen, an edict said: "The Western Capital Estate Office, Inner Palace Service, Palace Parks Office, Inner Gardens, and the other four offices—twenty-five hundred tax households under their patrol districts are all to be returned to prefecture and county control."
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen an edict returned twenty-five hundred tax households from four Western Capital palace offices to civil administration.

sentences.zh: 其廣德、升平二宮並停廢。

translations.literal: The Guangde and Shengping palaces were both abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangde and Shengping palaces were shut down.

sentences.zh: 應行從諸莊園林、亭殿、房舍、什物課利，宜令逐司依舊收管。」

translations.literal: Revenues from estates, gardens, pavilions, halls, houses, and goods used on imperial progresses should continue to be collected by each office as before."
translations.idiomatic: Progress-related estates and their revenues would remain under each office as before."

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙戌朔，日有食之，帝避正殿，百官守司。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on the bingxu new moon, there was a solar eclipse; the Emperor avoided the main hall and the officials kept their posts.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu new moon in the fourth month of summer, a solar eclipse occurred; the Emperor left the main hall and officials remained at their duties.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔停蔡州鄉軍。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict halted the Caizhou militia.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict disbanded the Caizhou militia.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以京師旱，分命群臣禱雨。

translations.literal: On wuzi, because the capital was in drought, various ministers were separately ordered to pray for rain.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, with drought in the capital, ministers were dispatched to pray for rain.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，制削奪慕容彥超在身官爵。

translations.literal: On guisi, by imperial decree Murong Yanchao's current offices and titles were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Murong Yanchao was stripped of all rank and title.

sentences.zh: 甲午，高麗國冊使、衛尉卿劉皞卒。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Liu Hao, envoy investing the King of Goryeo and Minister of the Guard, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Goryeo investiture envoy Liu Hao died.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔取來月五日，車駕赴兗州城下，慰勞將士。

translations.literal: On yimao, an edict set the fifth day of the coming month for the imperial carriage to go to Yanzhou below the walls to comfort the troops.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict scheduled the imperial visit to Yanzhou on the fifth of next month to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 以樞密副使鄭仁誨為右衛大將軍，依前充職，兼權大內都點檢；

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Zheng Renhui was made General of the Right Guards, continuing in his former post, and concurrently acting Chief Inspector of the Inner Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui was made Right Guards general, kept his military post, and named acting chief inner-palace inspector;

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、平章事、判三司李穀為權東京留守，兼判開封府事。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, and Commissioner of the Three Departments Li Gu was made acting Eastern Capital regent and concurrently administrator of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Gu became acting Eastern Capital regent and Kaifeng administrator.

sentences.zh: 五月丙辰朔，帝御崇元殿受朝，仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: On the bingchen new moon of the fifth month, the Emperor held court in the Chongyuan Hall with guards and insignia as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen new moon in the fifth month the Emperor held formal audience in the Chongyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 庚申，車駕發京師。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the imperial carriage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the Emperor left the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，至兗州城下。

translations.literal: On wuchen, he arrived below the walls of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he reached Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，收復兗州，斬慕容彥超，夷其族。

translations.literal: On yihai, Yanzhou was recovered; Murong Yanchao was beheaded and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Yanzhou fell; Murong Yanchao was executed and his clan wiped out.

sentences.zh: 詔端明殿學士顏衎權知兗州軍州事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Duanming Hall academician Yan Yan to act as administrator of Yanzhou military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Yan Yan acting Yanzhou administrator.

sentences.zh: 壬午，曲赦兗州管內罪人，取五月二十七日已前所犯罪，大辟已下，咸赦除之。

translations.literal: On renwu, a partial amnesty for criminals within Yanzhou jurisdiction: crimes committed before the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month, from capital offenses downward, were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu a partial amnesty pardoned all crimes in Yanzhou committed before the twenty-seventh of the fifth month, up to capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超徒黨，有逃避潛竄者，及城內將吏等並放罪。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao's partisans who had fled and hidden, and the officers and clerks within the city, were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao's followers in hiding and the city's officers were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 自慕容彥超違背以來，鄉州內有接便為非者，一切不問。

translations.literal: Since Murong Yanchao's rebellion, those in the countryside who had taken advantage to do wrong were not questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: Petty crimes committed in the countryside during the rebellion were overlooked.

sentences.zh: 諸軍將士歿於王事者，各與賻贈，都頭已上與贈官。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the armies who died in the imperial service each received funeral gifts; those of company head rank and above also received posthumous offices.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who died in service received funeral gifts; company heads and above received posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 兗州城內及官軍下寨四面去州五里內，今年所征夏秋稅及沿征錢物並放；

translations.literal: Within Yanzhou city and within five li on all sides of the imperial army camps, this year's summer and autumn taxes and all transit levies were remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Within Yanzhou and five li of the camps, summer and autumn taxes and transit levies were waived;

sentences.zh: 十里內，只放夏稅；

translations.literal: within ten li, only the summer tax was remitted;
translations.idiomatic: within ten li, only summer tax was remitted;

sentences.zh: 一州管界，今夏苗子三分放一分。

translations.literal: throughout the prefecture's jurisdiction, one-third of this summer's grain tax was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: and one-third of the summer grain levy was forgiven prefecture-wide.

sentences.zh: 城內百姓遭毀拆舍屋及遭燒焚者，給賜材木。

translations.literal: Commoners in the city whose houses had been demolished or burned were given timber.
translations.idiomatic: Residents whose homes were destroyed or burned received building timber.

sentences.zh: 諸處差到人夫內，有遭矢石死者，各給絹三匹，仍放戶下三年徭役雲。

translations.literal: Among corvée laborers dispatched from various places, those killed by arrows and stones each received three bolts of silk, and their households were exempted from corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée workers killed in battle received three bolts of silk, and their households were exempt from labor for three years.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔兗州降為防禦州，仍為望州。

translations.literal: On guiwei, an edict reduced Yanzhou to defense-prefecture status while retaining its rank as a premier prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Yanzhou was downgraded to a defense prefecture but kept premier status.

sentences.zh: 六月乙酉朔，帝幸曲阜縣，謁孔子祠。

translations.literal: On the yiyou new moon of the sixth month, the Emperor visited Qufu County and paid respects at the temple of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou new moon in the sixth month the Emperor visited Qufu and the temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 既奠，將致拜，左右曰：「仲尼，人臣也，無致拜。

translations.literal: After the offering, as he was about to perform a full bow, those beside him said: "Zhongni was a subject; there should be no full bow."
translations.idiomatic: After the offering, as he prepared to bow fully, attendants said: "Confucius was only a subject—no full bow is required."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「文宣王，百代帝王師也，得無敬乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The King of Culture and Propagation was teacher to emperors for a hundred generations—how could I not show reverence!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "The King of Culture was teacher to emperors for a hundred generations—how could I not revere him!"

sentences.zh: 」即拜奠於祠前。

translations.literal: He then bowed and made offering before the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and made offering before the shrine.

sentences.zh: 其所奠酒器、銀爐並留於祠所。

translations.literal: The wine vessels and silver brazier offered in sacrifice were all left at the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial wine vessels and silver brazier were left at the shrine.

sentences.zh: 遂幸孔林，拜孔子墓。

translations.literal: He then visited the Kong Family Grove and paid respects at Confucius's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He then visited the Kong Family Grove and bowed at Confucius's tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝謂近臣曰：「仲尼、亞聖之後，今有何人？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to his close officials: "Among the descendants of Zhongni, the Second Sage, who remains today?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked his close officials: "Who survives today among Confucius's line—the descendants of the Second Sage?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「前曲阜令、襲文宣公孔仁玉，是仲尼四十三代孫；

translations.literal: They replied: "The former magistrate of Qufu, inheritor Duke of Literary Completion Kong Renyu, is Confucius's forty-third-generation descendant;"
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "Former Qufu magistrate Kong Renyu, inheritor Duke of Literary Completion, is Confucius's forty-third-generation descendant;"

sentences.zh: 有鄉貢《三禮》顏涉，是顏淵之後。

translations.literal: There is also Yan She, a provincial recommendee in the Three Rites, who is a descendant of Yan Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Also among them is Yan She, who had submitted the Three Rites from his district and descends from Yan Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」即召見。

translations.literal: They were immediately summoned for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: They were summoned at once.

sentences.zh: 仁玉賜緋，口授曲阜令，顏涉授主簿，便令視事。

translations.literal: Renyu was granted scarlet robes, orally appointed magistrate of Qufu; Yan She was given the post of clerk, and both were ordered to take office at once.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu received scarlet robes and an oral appointment as Qufu magistrate; Yan She was made clerk; both were told to enter duty immediately.

sentences.zh: 仍敕兗州修葺孔子祠宇，墓側禁樵采。

translations.literal: An order was also issued to Yanzhou to repair Confucius's temple buildings, and woodcutting was forbidden beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was ordered to repair the Confucius temple, and gathering firewood at the tomb was banned.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，車駕還京。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以五月十三日至兗州，賊尚拒守，至十七日，晝夢道士一人進書，卷首云「車駕來月二日還京」，其下文字絕多，不能盡記。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had reached Yanzhou on the thirteenth day of the fifth month while the rebels still held out in defense; on the seventeenth day he dreamed in daytime of a Taoist presenting a book whose opening read, "The imperial carriage will return to the capital on the second of next month"; the text below was extremely long and could not all be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had reached Yanzhou on the thirteenth of the fifth month while rebels still held the city; on the seventeenth he dreamed by day that a Taoist brought a book opening with the words, "The Emperor returns to the capital on the second of next month"—the rest was too long to remember.

sentences.zh: 既寤，以夢告宰臣，又四日而城拔。

translations.literal: When he awoke he told the chief ministers of the dream, and four days later the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On waking he told the chief ministers; four days later the city fell.

sentences.zh: 帝至軍，凡駐蹕九日而賊平，果以六月二日發離城下，近代親征克捷，無如此之速也。

translations.literal: From the Emperor's arrival at the army until the rebels were subdued, he halted in camp nine days in all, and indeed set out from beneath the city walls on the second day of the sixth month—among personal campaigns of recent times that achieved victory, none had been so swift.
translations.idiomatic: From his arrival to victory he camped nine days, then left the city on the second of the sixth month as foretold—no personal campaign in recent memory had won so quickly.

sentences.zh: 是日大雨，城下行宮，水深數尺。

translations.literal: That day brought heavy rain; at the field palace below the city walls water stood several feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: That day heavy rain flooded the field palace below the walls to a depth of several feet.

sentences.zh: 其日晚，至中都縣，帝笑謂侍臣曰：「今日若不離城下，則當為潦所溺矣。

translations.literal: That evening he reached Zhongdu County; the Emperor said with a laugh to the attendants: "Had we not left the city today, we would have been drowned by the floodwaters."
translations.idiomatic: That evening at Zhongdu County the Emperor told his attendants with a laugh, "If we had not left the city today, the flood would have drowned us."

sentences.zh: 」戊戌，車駕至自兗州。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the imperial carriage arrived from Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Emperor returned from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以靈武節度使馮暉卒，輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: On xinchou, because Lingwu military governor Feng Hui had died, a day of court audience was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou court was canceled for a day in mourning after Lingwu military governor Feng Hui's death.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，前翰林學士李澣自契丹中上表，陳奏機事，且言偽幽州節度使蕭海貞欲謀向化，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: On renyin, former Hanlin Academician Li Huan submitted a memorial from within the Khitan realm, reporting on strategic affairs and saying that the puppet military governor of Youzhou, Xiao Haizhen, intended to seek allegiance to the court; the Emperor greatly commended this.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin former Hanlin academician Li Huan sent a memorial from Khitan territory reporting intelligence and claiming that Youzhou's puppet governor Xiao Haizhen wished to defect; the Emperor was much pleased.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李澣傳》：海貞與澣相善，澣乘間諷海貞以南歸之計，海貞納之。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Li Huan: Haizhen and Huan were on good terms; Huan seized an opportunity to suggest to Haizhen a plan to return south, and Haizhen accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: (Per the Song History biography of Li Huan: Haizhen and Huan were close; Huan seized a moment to urge a southern return, and Haizhen agreed.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，澣因定州孫方諫密表，言契丹衰微之勢，周祖嘉焉，遣諜者田重霸賫詔慰撫，仍命浣通信。

translations.literal: In Guangshun year 2 of Zhou, Huan sent a secret memorial through Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou describing the Khitan decline; Zhou Taizu praised this and sent the spy Tian Chongba with an imperial letter of reassurance, also ordering Huan to maintain correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Guangshun 2, Huan secretly memorialized via Dingzhou's Sun Fangjian on Khitan weakness; Taizu approved and sent the agent Tian Chongba with a comforting edict, ordering Huan to keep up communications.

sentences.zh: 澣復表述：「契丹主幼弱多寵，好擊鞠，大臣離貳，若出師討伐，因與通好，乃其時也。

translations.literal: Huan again reported: "The Khitan ruler is young and weak, much favored by courtiers, fond of cuju; the great ministers are divided and disloyal—if the army were sent to campaign against them and an alliance pursued in the same move, the time would be ripe."
translations.idiomatic: Huan added: "The Khitan ruler is young and pampered, addicted to cuju; ministers are split—if we march and offer friendship at once, the moment is right."

sentences.zh: 」屬中原多故，不能用其言。）〉

translations.literal: But the Central Plains were beset by many troubles, and his counsel could not be acted upon.")〉
translations.idiomatic: Turmoil in the Central Plains prevented the court from following his advice.")〉

sentences.zh: 癸卯，德妃董氏薨。

translations.literal: On guimao, Virtuous Consort Dong died.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Virtuous Consort Dong died.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔宣徽南院使袁鳷判開封府事。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict made Yuan Zhi, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, act as administrator of Kaifeng prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi an edict put Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Yuan Zhi in charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以朔方軍衙內都虞候馮繼業起復為朔方軍兵馬留後。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Feng Jiye, chief adjutant within the Shuofang Army headquarters, was recalled from mourning to be acting deputy for Shuofang Army troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Shuofang headquarters chief adjutant Feng Jiye was recalled from mourning as acting Shuofang army deputy.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，幸舊宅，為德妃舉哀故也。

translations.literal: On jiayin, he visited his old residence, because mourning was being held for the Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he visited his old residence to mourn the Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙辰，詔：「內外臣僚，每遇永壽節，舊設齋供。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on bingchen, an edict said: "Within and outside the court, whenever the Eternal Longevity Festival occurs, vegetarian offerings were formerly set out.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the seventh month of autumn an edict ruled: "When the Eternal Longevity Festival comes, officials inside and outside court had each held separate vegetarian offerings.

sentences.zh: 今後中書門下與文武百官共設一齋，侍衛親軍都指揮使已下共設一齋，樞密使、內諸司使已下共設一齋，其餘前任職員及諸司職掌，更不得開設道場及設齋。

translations.literal: Henceforth the Secretariat-Chancellery and civil and military officials are to hold one offering together; the commanders-in-chief of the palace guard and imperial guard and those below them are to hold one offering together; the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, commissioners of the inner bureaus, and those below them are to hold one offering together; all other former officeholders and clerks of the various bureaus may no longer open prayer halls or set out offerings."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Secretariat and all civil and military officials will share one offering; palace and imperial guard commanders and below will share one; the military affairs commissioner and inner bureau commissioners and below will share one; other former officials and bureau staff may no longer hold prayer halls or offerings."

sentences.zh: 」是日大風雨，破屋拔樹，尚書省都堂有龍穿屋壞獸角而去，西壁有爪跡存焉。

translations.literal: That day brought great wind and rain; houses were destroyed and trees uprooted. In the main hall of the Department of State Affairs a dragon pierced the roof, broke the beast-ornament, and departed; claw marks remained on the west wall.
translations.idiomatic: That day violent wind and rain wrecked houses and uprooted trees; a dragon was said to have burst through the State Affairs main hall, broke a roof beast ornament, and left claw marks on the west wall.

sentences.zh: 襄州大水。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou suffered great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou was flooded.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔復升陳州、曹州為節鎮。

translations.literal: On dingmao, an edict restored Chenzhou and Caozhou to circuit military commission status.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao an edict restored Chenzhou and Caozhou to full military circuits.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使、洋州節度使郭崇為陳州節度使，以侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英為曹州節度使，並典軍如故。

translations.literal: Palace guard cavalry commander-in-chief and Yangzhou military governor Guo Chong was made military governor of Chenzhou; palace guard infantry commander-in-chief Cao Ying was made military governor of Caozhou; both continued to command armies as before.
translations.idiomatic: Palace cavalry commander and Yangzhou governor Guo Chong became Chenzhou governor; infantry commander Cao Ying became Caozhou governor; both kept their army commands.

sentences.zh: 以陳州防禦使藥元福為晉州節度使。

translations.literal: Chenzhou defense commissioner Yao Yuanfu was made military governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chenzhou defense commissioner Yao Yuanfu was appointed Jinzhou military governor.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔相州節度使李筠權知潞州軍州事。

translations.literal: On xinwei, an edict made Xiangzhou military governor Li Jun temporarily administer Lu Prefecture military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei an edict put Xiangzhou governor Li Jun in temporary charge of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以小底都指揮使、漢州刺史李重進為大內都點檢兼馬步都軍頭，領恩州團練使；

translations.literal: On bingzi, Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Palace Inner Corps and military governor of Hanzhou, was made chief inspector of the Great Inner Palace and concurrently commander-in-chief of both cavalry and infantry armies, and given charge of En Prefecture as regimental trainer;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Hanzhou governor and palace inner corps commander Li Chongjin became chief inner-palace inspector and cavalry-infantry commander-in-chief, with Enzhou as regimental trainer;

sentences.zh: 以內殿直都知、駙馬都尉張永德領和州刺史，充小底第一軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Inner Palace Directorate intendant and Imperial Son-in-law Commander Zhang Yongde was given charge of He Prefecture as prefect and appointed commander-in-chief of the First Army of the Palace Inner Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Directorate intendant and imperial son-in-law Zhang Yongde took Hezhou and became commander of the First Palace Inner Corps Army.

sentences.zh: 八月甲申朔，翰林學士、刑部尚書張沆落職守本官。

translations.literal: On the jiashen new moon of the eighth month, Hanlin Academician and Minister of Punishments Zhang Hong was removed from his academic post and retained his original office.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth-month jiashen new moon Hanlin academician and minister of punishments Zhang Hong was stripped of his Hanlin post but kept his ministry.

sentences.zh: 以中書舍人、史館修撰判館事徐臺符為禮部尚書，充翰林學士承旨；

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter and History Bureau compiler-administrator Xu Taifu was made Minister of Rites and appointed Hanlin Academician in Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter and history bureau administrator Xu Taifu became minister of rites and chief Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎韋勛為尚書右丞；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Wei Xun was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Vice minister of war Wei Xun became right vice director of state affairs;

sentences.zh: 以尚書右丞於德辰為吏部侍郎；

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yu Dechen was made Vice Minister of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director Yu Dechen became vice minister of personnel;

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎邊歸讜為兵部侍郎；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Bian Guichan was made Vice Minister of War;
translations.idiomatic: Revenue vice minister Bian Guichan became war vice minister;

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎趙上交為戶部侍郎；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Zhao Shangjiao was made Vice Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Rites vice minister Zhao Shangjiao became revenue vice minister;

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士、左散騎常侍陳觀為工部侍郎，依前充職；

translations.literal: Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Chen Guan was made Vice Minister of Works, continuing in his former post as before;
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs direct academician and left cavalry attendant Chen Guan became works vice minister while keeping his former post;

sentences.zh: 以刑部侍郎景範為左司郎中，充樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments Jing Fan was made Left Section Director and appointed Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments vice minister Jing Fan became left section director and military affairs direct academician.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，樞密使王峻上章，請解樞衡，凡三上章，詔不允。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun submitted a memorial requesting release from the pivot of state power; he submitted three memorials in all, and edicts refused each time.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou military affairs commissioner Wang Jun three times memorialized to resign; each time the court refused.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，潁州奏，先於淮南俘獲孳畜，已準詔送還本土。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Yingzhou reported livestock seized earlier in Huainan had been returned to their homeland as the edict ordered.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Yingzhou reported that livestock captured in Huainan had been sent home per edict.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔止絕吏民詣闕舉請刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: On jiawu, an edict forbade officials and commoners from coming to the palace to petition for the appointment of prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu an edict barred officials and commoners from petitioning at court for prefect and magistrate appointments.

sentences.zh: 賜宰臣李穀白藤肩輿。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Gu was granted a white rattan sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Li Gu received a white rattan sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 時穀以今年七月，因步履傷臂，請告數旬，詔穀扶持三司，刻名印署事，仍放朝參。

translations.literal: At the time, in the seventh month of this year, Gu had injured his arm while walking and requested leave for several tens of days; an edict ordered Gu, supported, to oversee the Three Departments, affix his engraved name seal to affairs, and he was exempted from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: That July Gu had hurt his arm walking and took leave for weeks; an edict let him run the Three Departments with seal authority while excusing him from court.

sentences.zh: 庚子，潞州節度使常思移鎮宋州，相州節度使李筠移鎮潞州。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Luzhou military governor Chang Si transferred his military commission to Song Prefecture; Xiangzhou military governor Li Jun transferred his military commission to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Luzhou's Chang Si moved to Songzhou and Xiangzhou's Li Jun moved to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，鄆州節度使高行周薨。

translations.literal: On renyin, Yunzhou military governor Gao Xingzhou died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Yunzhou military governor Gao Xingzhou died.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔改鹽曲法，鹽曲犯五斤已上處死，煎鹼鹽者犯一斤已上處死。

translations.literal: On guichou, an edict revised the law on salt yeast: offenders with five jin or more of salt yeast were put to death; those who boiled alkaline salt, with one jin or more, were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou an edict tightened salt-yeast law: five jin or more of yeast merited death; one jin or more of illicit boiled salt merited death.

sentences.zh: 先是，漢法不計斤兩多少，並處極刑，至是始革之。

translations.literal: Earlier, under Han law no weight threshold applied—all were punished by extreme penalty; only now was this reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law any amount had meant capital punishment; now thresholds were set for the first time.

sentences.zh: 九月庚午，以大理卿劇可久為太僕卿，以左庶子張仁彖為大理卿，以司天監趙延乂為太府卿兼判司天監事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengwu, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Ju Kejiu was made Chief of the Imperial Stud; Left Subdirector of the Heir Apparent's Household Zhang Renbiao was made Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Director of the Astronomy Bureau Zhao Yanyi was made Chief of the Imperial Storehouse and concurrently administrator of Astronomy Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the ninth month judicial review chief Ju Kejiu became imperial stud chief; left heir-apparent subdirector Zhang Renbiao took judicial review; astronomy director Zhao Yanyi became imperial storehouse chief and also ran the astronomy bureau.

sentences.zh: 詔北面沿邊州鎮，自守疆埸，不得入北界俘掠。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the northern frontier prefectures and garrisons along the border to defend their own boundaries and not enter the northern realm to capture and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told northern border circuits to hold their own lines and not raid into Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，鎮州奏，契丹寇深、冀州，遣龍捷都指揮使劉誨、牙內都指揮使何繼筠等率兵拒之而退。

translations.literal: On yihai, Zhenzhou reported that the Khitan raided Shen and Ji prefectures; Dragon Swift commander-in-chief Liu Hui, Inner Headquarters chief adjutant He Jiyun, and others led troops to resist and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Zhenzhou reported Khitan raids on Shen and Ji; Liu Hui, He Jiyun, and others drove them off.

sentences.zh: 時契丹聞官軍至，掠冀部丁壯數百隨行，狼狽而北，冀部被擄者望見官軍，鼓噪不已，官軍不敢進，其丁壯盡為蕃軍所殺而去。

translations.literal: At the time, when the Khitan heard the imperial army had arrived, they seized several hundred able-bodied men of Ji Prefecture to accompany them north in disarray; the captives of Ji Prefecture, seeing the imperial army, shouted without cease, but the imperial army dared not advance, and all those men were killed by the barbarian army before they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the imperial army approach, the Khitan dragged hundreds of Ji men north in disorder; the captives cheered at sight of the army, but imperial troops dared not advance, and the Khitan slaughtered every captive before fleeing.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以鄭州防禦使白重贊為相州留後。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Zhengzhou defense commissioner Bai Chongzan was made acting commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Zhengzhou defense commissioner Bai Chongzan became acting Xiangzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，樂壽都監杜延熙奏，於瀛州南殺敗契丹，斬首三百級，獲馬四十七匹。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Leshou garrison supervisor Du Yanxi reported defeating the Khitan south of Ying Prefecture, beheading three hundred, and capturing forty-seven horses.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Leshou supervisor Du Yanxi reported defeating Khitan south of Yingzhou—three hundred heads and forty-seven horses.

sentences.zh: 癸未，帝姨母韓氏追封楚國夫人，故第四姊追封福慶長公主。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Emperor's maternal aunt Lady Han was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Chu State; his late fourth elder sister was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Emperor's maternal aunt Lady Han was posthumously made Lady of Chu; his late fourth sister became Grand Princess Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 癸未，易州奏，契丹武州刺史石越來奔。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Yizhou reported that Shi Yue, prefect of Wuzhou under the Khitan, had come over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Yizhou reported Khitan Wuzhou prefect Shi Yue had defected.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙戌，以前晉州節度使王彥超為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on bingxu, former Jinzhou military governor Wang Yanchao was made military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the tenth month of winter former Jinzhou governor Wang Yanchao became Heyang military governor.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔：「諸州罷任或朝覲，並不得以器械進貢。

translations.literal: On gengyin, an edict said: "When prefects leave office or come to court for an audience, none may present weapons as tribute."
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin an edict ruled: "Departing or audience-bound prefects may no longer offer weapons as tribute."

sentences.zh: 」先是，諸道州府，各有作院，每月課造軍器，逐季搬送京師進納。

translations.literal: Earlier, each circuit prefecture and district had its own manufacture office, assigning monthly production of military equipment, shipping quarterly to the capital for delivery and submission.
translations.idiomatic: Previously every circuit had workshops that monthly produced arms and quarterly shipped them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其逐州每年占留系省錢帛不少，謂之「甲料」，仍更於部內廣配土產物，征斂數倍，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Each prefecture annually retained no small portion of funds and silks tied to the central provinces, called "armor materials"; moreover within their jurisdictions they widely levied local products at several times the rate—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures kept large "armor material" shares of provincial funds and levied local goods at multiples—the people bore heavy burdens.

sentences.zh: 除上供軍器外，節度使、刺史又私造器甲，以進貢為名，功費又倍，悉取之於民。

translations.literal: Beyond weapons submitted as tribute to the center, military governors and prefects also privately made armor and weapons, under the name of tribute presentation—the cost again doubled, all taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Besides mandated arms, governors and prefects privately forged armor under the guise of tribute, doubling costs again—all from the people.

sentences.zh: 帝以諸州器甲造作不精，兼占留屬省物用過當，乃令罷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because weapons and armor made in the prefectures were not finely crafted and retention of provincial goods was excessive, ordered these practices abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Finding prefectural arms poorly made and provincial withholdings excessive, the Emperor abolished the workshops.

sentences.zh: 仍選擇諸道作工，赴京作坊，以備役使。

translations.literal: Craftsmen from the various circuits were also selected and sent to capital workshops to serve as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Selected craftsmen from the circuits were sent to capital workshops for imperial service.

sentences.zh: 乙未，永興軍奏，宣徽北院使、知軍府事翟光鄴卒。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Yongxing Army reported that Zhai Guangye, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and administrator of army headquarters affairs, had died.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Yongxing reported Northern Palace Secretariat commissioner and army administrator Zhai Guangye had died.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，葬德妃，廢朝。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Virtuous Consort was buried; court was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Virtuous Consort was buried and court was canceled.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以宣徽南院使袁鳷權知永興軍府事，以樞密直學士、工部侍郎陳觀權知開封府事。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Yuan Zhi, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made acting administrator of Yongxing Army headquarters affairs; Chen Guan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Works, was made acting administrator of Kaifeng prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Yuan Zhi acted for Yongxing; military affairs academician and works vice minister Chen Guan acted for Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 己亥，升鉅野縣為濟州。

translations.literal: On jihai, Juye County was promoted to Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Juye County was elevated to Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以樞密院副使鄭仁誨為宣徽北院使兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zheng Renhui was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs vice commissioner Zheng Renhui became Northern Palace Secretariat commissioner with a concurrent vice military affairs post.

sentences.zh: 庚子，幸樞密院，王峻請之也。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he visited the Bureau of Military Affairs—it was at Wang Jun's request.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he visited the Bureau of Military Affairs at Wang Jun's invitation.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，宰臣李穀以臂傷未愈，上表辭位，凡三上章，詔報不允。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Chief Minister Li Gu, his arm wound not yet healed, submitted a memorial resigning his post; he submitted three memorials in all, and edict replies refused.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen chief minister Li Gu, still injured, thrice memorialized to resign; the court refused each time.

sentences.zh: 丁未，滄州奏，自十月已前，蕃歸漢戶萬九千八百戶。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Cangzhou reported that before the tenth month, barbarian households returning to Han numbered nineteen thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Cangzhou reported 19,800 barbarian households had returned to Han rule before the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 是時，北境饑謹，人民轉徙，繈負而歸中土者，散居河北州縣，凡數十萬口。

translations.literal: At this time the northern frontier suffered famine; people migrated, and those bearing infants on their backs who returned to the Central Realm were scattered across the prefectures and counties of Hebei—altogether several hundreds of thousands of persons.
translations.idiomatic: Northern famine sent refugees south; families with infants in arms scattered across Hebei by the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，荊南奏，朗州大將劉言，以今年十月三日領兵趨長沙，十五日至潭州，淮南所署湖南節度使邊鎬、岳州刺史宋德權並棄城遁去。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Jingnan reported that Liu Yan, a great general of Lang Prefecture, on the third day of the tenth month of this year led troops toward Changsha, reached Tan Prefecture on the fifteenth, and Huainan's appointed military governor of Hunan Bian Hao and Yue Prefecture prefect Song Dequan both abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the eleventh month Jingnan reported that Langzhou general Liu Yan marched on Changsha on the third of the tenth month, reached Tanzhou on the fifteenth, and Huainan's Hunan governor Bian Hao and Yuezhou prefect Song Dequan fled their posts.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以前少府監馬從斌為殿中監。

translations.literal: On gengshen, former Director of the Palace Manufactories Ma Congbin was made Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen former palace manufactories director Ma Congbin became palace domestic service director.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，樞密使王峻亡妻崔氏追封趙國夫人，非故事也。

translations.literal: On renxu, Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun's deceased wife Lady Cui was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Zhao State—it was without precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Wang Jun's late wife Lady Cui was posthumously made Lady of Zhao—without precedent.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，刑部尚書張沆卒。

translations.literal: On yichou, Minister of Punishments Zhang Hong died.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou minister of punishments Zhang Hong died.

sentences.zh: 辛未，陜州折從阮移鎮邠州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, She Congruan of Shaan Prefecture transferred his military commission to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Shaan's She Congruan moved to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 以前宋州節度使李洪義為安州節度使。

translations.literal: Former Songzhou military governor Li Hongyi was made military governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Former Songzhou governor Li Hongyi became Anzhou military governor.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，青州符彥卿移鎮鄆州。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Fu Yanqing of Qing Prefecture transferred his military commission to Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Qingzhou's Fu Yanqing moved to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔曰：「累朝已來，用兵不息，至於繕治甲胄，未免配役生靈，多取於民，助成軍器。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict said: "From successive reigns onward warfare has never ceased; as for maintaining armor, corvée of the people could not be avoided—much was taken from the people to supply military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu an edict declared: "For generations war has never stopped; maintaining armor meant drafting the people—too much was taken from them to arm the armies."

sentences.zh: 就中皮革，尤峻科刑，稍犯嚴條，皆抵極典，鄉縣以之生事，奸猾得以侵漁，宜立新規，用革前弊。

translations.literal: Among these, leather was especially subject to severe punishments; any slight breach of strict statutes met the extreme penalty. Prefectures and counties used this to create trouble, and the cunning exploited it to extort—new regulations should be established to reform former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Leather laws were especially harsh—minor violations brought capital punishment; local officials abused them and rackets flourished—new rules were needed to end the abuse.

sentences.zh: 應天下所納牛皮，今將逐所納數，三分內減二分，其一分於人戶苗畝上配定。

translations.literal: For ox hides submitted empire-wide, of each submission two-thirds will now be reduced, with the remaining one-third apportioned per household on cultivated acreage.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide ox-hide levies would drop by two-thirds; the remaining third would be fixed per household by acreage.

sentences.zh: 每秋夏苗共十頃納連角皮一張，其黃牛納幹筋四兩，水牛半斤，犢子皮不在納限。

translations.literal: Every ten qing of summer and autumn crop fields required one hide with horns attached; for yellow cattle four liang of dried sinew, for water buffalo half a jin; calf hides were not within the levy limit.
translations.idiomatic: Ten qing of summer and autumn fields owed one horned hide; yellow cattle owed four liang of dried sinew, water buffalo half a jin; calf hides were exempt.

sentences.zh: 牛馬驢騾皮筋角，今後官中更不禁斷，只不得將出化外敵境。

translations.literal: Ox, horse, donkey, and mule hides, sinew, and horn—hereafter the government will no longer prohibit them, but they may not be taken out beyond the frontier into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hides, sinew, and horn from cattle and pack animals would no longer be banned domestically, but export beyond the frontier was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 州縣先置巡檢牛皮節級並停。

translations.literal: Leather-inspector patrol posts and rank posts formerly established in prefectures and counties were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural leather-inspector patrols were abolished.

sentences.zh: 」丙子，詔曰：「應內外文武官僚幕職、州縣官舉選人等，今後有父母、祖父母亡歿未經遷葬者，其主家之長，不得輒求仕進，所由司亦不得申舉解送。

translations.literal: On bingzi, an edict said: "All civil and military officials, staff, prefectural and county officers, and examination candidates—hereafter if parents or grandparents have died and not yet been reburied, the head of the household may not rashly seek advancement in office, and the responsible offices may not recommend or forward them."
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi an edict barred civil and military officials, staff, local officers, and examination candidates whose parents or grandparents remained unburied from seeking or receiving office.

sentences.zh: 如是卑幼在下者，不在此限。

translations.literal: If junior members of the family rank below, they are not within this restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Junior family members below the household head were exempt.

sentences.zh: 」己卯，日南至，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: On jimao, the winter solstice, the Emperor received court congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall with guard formations according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the winter solstice, the Emperor received congratulations at Chongyuan Hall with full ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙戌，權武平軍留後劉言遣牙將張崇嗣入奏，於十月十三日，與節度副使王進逵、行軍司馬何敬貞、指揮使周行逢等，同共部領戰棹，攻收湖南，偽節度使邊鎬當夜出奔，王進逵等已入潭州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army, sent adjutant general Zhang Chongsi to report to court that on the thirteenth day of the tenth month, together with vice military governor Wang Jinkui, campaign chief of staff He Jingzhen, commander Zhou Xingfeng, and others, they jointly led war boats, attacked and recovered Hunan; the puppet military governor Bian Hao fled that same night, and Wang Jinkui and the others had already entered Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the twelfth month acting Wuiping deputy Liu Yan sent adjutant Zhang Chongsi to report: on the thirteenth of the tenth month he, vice governor Wang Jinkui, chief of staff He Jingzhen, commander Zhou Xingfeng, and others led war boats to retake Hunan; puppet governor Bian Hao fled that night and Wang Jinkui entered Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王逵傳》：逵，朗州武陵人，或名進逵。

translations.literal: (Chronicles of the Nine States, Biography of Wang Kui: Kui was a native of Wuling in Lang Prefecture, also called Jinkui.
translations.idiomatic: (Per the Chronicles of the Nine States biography of Wang Kui: Kui was from Wuling in Langzhou, also known as Jinkui.

sentences.zh: 邊鎬為武安軍節度使，召劉言入覲，言不行，謀於逵曰：「江南召我，不往，必加兵於我矣，為之奈何！

translations.literal: Bian Hao served as military governor of the Wu'an Army and summoned Liu Yan to court for an audience; Yan did not go and consulted Kui, saying: "The Jiangnan court summons me—if I do not go, they will surely send troops against me. What is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao, Wu'an Army governor, summoned Liu Yan to court; Yan refused and asked Kui: "If Jiangnan summons me and I stay away, they will attack—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」逵曰：「鎬之此來，以制置潭、朗為名，公如速行，正入其算。

translations.literal: Kui said: "Hao comes on the pretext of administering Tan and Lang. If you go quickly, you walk straight into his plan."
translations.idiomatic: Kui replied: "Hao's mission is to control Tan and Lang—if you hurry to court, you play into his hand."

sentences.zh: 武陵負江湖之阻，帶甲百萬，乃欲拱手臣異姓乎？

translations.literal: Wuling lies behind the barrier of rivers and lakes, with a million armed men—will you simply bow and submit to a surname not your own?"
translations.idiomatic: "Wuling has rivers for defense and a million men under arms—will you meekly bow to outsiders?"

sentences.zh: 鎬新至長沙，經略未定，乘人心憤怒，引兵攻鎬，可一鼓而擒也。

translations.literal: Hao has newly reached Changsha and his control is not yet settled; seize this moment while hearts are angry, lead troops to attack Hao, and he can be taken in a single assault.
translations.idiomatic: Hao has just reached Changsha and is unsettled—strike while men are angry, attack Hao, and you can take him in one rush.

sentences.zh: 」言然之，乃遣與何景真等同起兵於武陵，號十指揮使，以攻邊鎬。

translations.literal: Yan agreed, then sent him together with He Jingzhen and others to raise troops at Wuling, styling themselves Ten-Command Commanders to attack Bian Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan agreed and dispatched him with He Jingzhen and others to raise troops at Wuling under the title Ten-Command Commander, to attack Bian Hao.

sentences.zh: 逵率舟師南上，至長沙，邊鎬大駭，以所部奔歸江南，諸州屯守皆罷之，盡復湖外之地。）〉

translations.literal: Kui led a fleet south to Changsha; Bian Hao was greatly terrified, fled with his division back to Jiangnan, garrison posts in all prefectures were abolished, and all lands beyond the lakes were recovered.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Kui led his fleet south to Changsha; terrified, Bian Hao fled with his troops back to Jiangnan, garrisons in every prefecture were withdrawn, and all territory beyond the lakes was recovered.)〉

sentences.zh: 癸巳，太子太師致仕安叔千卒。

translations.literal: On guisi, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent An Shuqian died.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, An Shuqian, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔今後諸侯入朝，不得進奉買宴。

translations.literal: On jiawu, an edict said that hereafter when feudatory lords came to court they might not present tribute to purchase banquets.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, an edict forbade feudatory lords who came to court from presenting tribute to purchase banquets.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，皇子澶州節度使榮落起復，加同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Prince Rong, military governor of Cao Prefecture, left mourning restoration and was made co-equal Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Prince Rong, military governor of Cao Prefecture, left mourning restoration and was appointed co-equal Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，太子少傅致仕王延卒。

translations.literal: On wuxu, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wang Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Wang Yan, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，幸西莊。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以端明殿學士顏衎權知開封府事。

translations.literal: On yisi, Palace Attendant Academician Yan Kan was made acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Palace Attendant Academician Yan Kan was appointed acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史臺奏：「請改左右衛復為左右屯衛。

translations.literal: The Censorate submitted: "We request that the Left and Right Guards be changed back to the Left and Right Garrison Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate submitted: "We request that the Left and Right Guards be restored to the Left and Right Garrison Guards.

sentences.zh: 」從之，避御名也。

translations.literal: The request was granted, to avoid the imperial taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, to avoid the imperial taboo name.

sentences.zh: 是冬無雪。

translations.literal: That winter there was no snow.
translations.idiomatic: That winter brought no snow.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年春正月壬子朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: On the renyin new moon of the first month in spring, Guangshun year 3, the Emperor received court congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall with guard formations according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin new moon of the first month of spring, Guangshun 3, the Emperor received New Year congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall with full ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 幸太平宮起居漢太后。

translations.literal: He visited the Taiping Palace to pay respects to the Han Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the Taiping Palace to pay his respects to the Han Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，賜群臣射於內鞠場。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the ministers were granted archery at the inner ball-court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Emperor granted the ministers an archery session at the inner ball-court.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，武平軍兵馬留後劉言奏：「潭州干戈之後，焚燒殆盡，乞移使府於武陵。

translations.literal: On yimao, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army, submitted: "After the fighting at Tan Prefecture, it has been burned nearly clean; we beg to move the commissioner headquarters to Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army, submitted: "After the war at Tanzhou, the city has been burned nearly to ashes; we beg to move the commissioner headquarters to Wuling.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 詔升朗州為大都督府，在潭州之上。

translations.literal: An edict elevated Lang Prefecture to a Grand Protectorate, ranking above Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict elevated Langzhou to a Grand Protectorate, ranking above Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以武平軍節度使留後、檢校太尉劉言為檢校太師、同平章事，行朗州大都督，充武平軍節度兼三司水陸轉運等使，制置武安、靜江等軍事，進封彭城郡公；

translations.literal: On bingchen, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army military governor and honorary Grand Guardian, was made honorary Grand Preceptor and co-equal Grand Councilor, acting Grand Protector of Lang Prefecture, appointed military governor of the Wuiping Army concurrently with Commissioner of the Three Offices' Overland and Water Transport, with authority over Wu'an and Jingjiang military affairs, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Pengcheng Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army and honorary Grand Guardian, was made honorary Grand Preceptor and co-equal Grand Councilor, acting Grand Protector of Langzhou, appointed military governor of the Wuiping Army and Commissioner of the Three Offices' Overland and Water Transport, given authority over Wu'an and Jingjiang military affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng Commandery;

sentences.zh: 武平軍節度副使、權知潭州軍州事、檢校太傅王進逵為檢校太尉，行潭州刺史，充武安軍節度使；

translations.literal: Wang Jinkui, vice military governor of the Wuiping Army, acting administrator of Tan Prefecture military and prefectural affairs, and honorary Grand Mentor, was made honorary Grand Guardian, acting prefect of Tan Prefecture, and appointed military governor of the Wu'an Army;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinkui, vice military governor of the Wuiping Army and acting administrator of Tanzhou, was made honorary Grand Guardian, acting prefect of Tanzhou, and appointed military governor of the Wu'an Army;

sentences.zh: 以武安軍行軍司馬兼衙內步軍都指揮使、檢校太傅何敬貞為檢校太尉，行桂州刺史，充靜江軍節度使；

translations.literal: He Jingzhen, campaign chief of staff of the Wu'an Army and concurrently commander-in-chief of the inner palace infantry and honorary Grand Mentor, was made honorary Grand Guardian, acting prefect of Gui Prefecture, and appointed military governor of the Jingjiang Army;
translations.idiomatic: He Jingzhen, Wu'an Army campaign chief of staff and commander-in-chief of the inner palace infantry, was made honorary Grand Guardian, acting prefect of Guizhou, and appointed military governor of the Jingjiang Army;

sentences.zh: 以張仿領眉州刺史，充武平軍節度副使；

translations.literal: Zhang Fang was given nominal appointment as prefect of Mei Prefecture and appointed vice military governor of the Wuiping Army;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang was given nominal appointment as prefect of Meizhou and appointed vice military governor of the Wuiping Army;

sentences.zh: 以朱元琇領黃州刺史，充靜江軍節度副使；

translations.literal: Zhu Yuanxiu was given nominal appointment as prefect of Huang Prefecture and appointed vice military governor of the Jingjiang Army;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuanxiu was given nominal appointment as prefect of Huangzhou and appointed vice military governor of the Jingjiang Army;

sentences.zh: 以周行逢領集州刺史，充武安軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingfeng was given nominal appointment as prefect of Ji Prefecture and appointed campaign chief of staff of the Wu'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng was given nominal appointment as prefect of Jizhou and appointed campaign chief of staff of the Wu'an Army.

sentences.zh: 自進逵而下，皆劉言將校也。

translations.literal: From Jinkui downward, all were Liu Yan's commanders and officers.
translations.idiomatic: From Jinkui on down, all were Liu Yan's commanders and officers.

sentences.zh: 邠州奏，慶州略蕃部野雞族略奪商旅，侵擾州界。

translations.literal: Bin Prefecture reported that the Yejie tribe of Fan peoples in Qing Prefecture's border regions plundered traveling merchants and harassed the prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhou reported that the Yejie tribe on Qingzhou's frontier had plundered traveling merchants and harassed the prefectural border.

sentences.zh: 詔遣寧州刺史張建武等率兵掩襲，仍先賜敕書安撫，如不從命，即進軍問罪。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Ning Prefecture inspector Zhang Jianwu and others to lead troops in a surprise attack, yet first granted an imperial letter to pacify them; if they did not obey, they were to advance and punish them.
